findings.text: Registration entry points add and remove a caller supplied notifier block from a shared blocking chain used around lazy vmap purging, returning the chain helper result to the caller.
A dedicated mutex serializes lazy area reclamation; the periodic work handler holds it across a single maximal purge request that declines forced flushing.
The KASAN release batching limit is thirty two entries.
The total vmalloc extent has two build variants, one of one hundred twenty eight megabytes and another of one hundred twenty eight gigabytes.

Sizing derives total pages from the vmalloc extent divided by page size, caps a single small mapping at bits per word, bounds the per block bitmap between twice that cap and one thousand twenty four, clamps the effective bitmap using total pages divided by rounded CPU count and sixteen, and sizes a block as bitmap bits times page size, with small helpers selecting the lesser and greater of two values.

Small mapping flags use value one to mark ram mappings and value two to mark block managed mappings, with mask value three covering both, and the purge threshold is one quarter of the block bitmap size.

The per CPU queue layout carries a spin guard plus a list of blocks retaining free space plus an indexed container of blocks, with commentary noting the container needs dynamic memory and could be replaced by a tree.

A block descriptor carries its own spin guard, a back pointer to its area, free and dirty page counters, a bitmap of used slots sized by the block bitmap constant, a dirty interval expressed as minimum and maximum offsets, list links for free membership and purging, a deferred reclamation callback head, and an owning CPU number.
The PFN mapping helper carries an array of frame numbers plus target protections plus a cursor index that advances as each entry is installed.
The setup helper fully links a new descriptor and area: flags and caller are stored, address comes from area start, both size fields take the area extent, and the area points back to the descriptor.
Block queues exist as one instance per processor, so allocation fast paths use the local processor queue.
Block virtual addresses add a page offset scaled by page shift to the block base and are constrained to remain inside the same block index.

Block creation allocates a descriptor on the local node, reserves an aligned block sized area tagged as ram and block, initializes guard and counters with the first extent marked used and dirty interval empty, inserts the descriptor into the address indexed store, and publishes it on the owning CPU free list; any area or index failure releases what was taken and reports an error pointer.

Small allocation rejects unaligned or oversize or empty sizes, converts size to an order, scans the local free list under read side protection skipping blocks lacking room, then under block guard claims a suffix extent and marks its bitmap and possibly unlinks the block when exhausted, falling back to creating a new block when no candidate supplied an address.

Small release validates size, flushes cache coverage, clears the corresponding bitmap extent, tears down the page range without flushing, flushes the TLB only when debug page allocation is active, expands the dirty interval and dirty count, and either releases the whole block when every slot became dirty or retains it for reuse.

Ram mapping chooses the block allocator for counts within the small limit and a dedicated area otherwise, installs the supplied pages with kernel protections, unwinds on mapping failure, and scrubs tags and poison state; unmapping mirrors the split, validates range and alignment, poisons, and either returns the extent to the block layer or unlinks and frees the dedicated area, while a separate entry flushes all aliases with maximal range.
Area reservation helpers request a full vmalloc range area of caller size with single page alignment, differing only in whether the recorded caller is implicit or explicit.

Early boot keeps a simple sorted list anchored in init memory; insertion keeps address order and rejects overlaps, while registration scans for the first aligned gap large enough, fails if beyond the vmalloc end, links the descriptor, and prepares early shadow coverage, with both paths forbidden after initialization completes.

The page array mapper sleeps, rejects reset permission requests and strips any no guard request, refuses counts beyond total memory, reserves an area, installs pages without execute rights, unwinds on failure, and optionally records the backing array and count for later release.

The frame number mapper reserves an IO style area sized by count, installs each entry as a special mapping under init context while advancing a cursor and rejecting entries that correspond to valid memory, flushes cache coverage on success, and frees the area on failure.

Three deferred handlers drain queued work: one serializes lazy purging under the purge mutex, one releases every node from a deferred free list, and one reclaims pending areas choosing direct area release when no pages are attached and generic release otherwise.

Node aware allocation wrappers provide plain, zeroing, huge capable, user mapped with shared alignment and zeroing, node pinned, and low thirty two bit variants, delegating to ranged helpers with kernel protections and recorded caller.

Reallocation with size zero frees and returns null, with null input behaves as fresh allocation, otherwise looks up the existing area and validates alignment and node affinity; shrinking updates requested size with optional clearing and possibly unmaps and frees tail pages when crossing page boundaries except for huge or permission resetting or user mapped or filesystem constrained cases; growth within already mapped pages only updates requested size; larger growth allocates anew, copies the smaller of old and new sizes, frees the old extent, and reports allocation failure as null.

Diagnostic read helpers copy page by page through fault safe primitives, substituting zeroes for unmapped pages or holes between used extents, holding the block guard while scanning used intervals and accepting unsynchronized mapping teardown rather than burdening allocation paths with extra locking.

Callers face hard checks and warnings for empty, oversize, unaligned, out of range, or unknown areas, for guard suppression and permission reset misuse, for excessive map counts, for degraded alignment growth, for mismatched recorded sizes, and for attempts to map valid frames as special.

Block layer locking nests read side traversal of free lists outside per block guards, takes the queue guard only to unlink exhausted blocks or to publish new ones with deferred list primitives safe under migration, uses the block guard for bitmap and counter updates including dirty interval expansion, and uses a node busy guard when shrinking recorded page counts against concurrent readers.

The vmalloc flag mask allows sleepable allocation together with atomic plus also no wait plus also no fail plus also zeroing plus also no retry plus also retry may fail plus also filesystem less plus also IO less plus also accounted kernel plus also user plus also no lockdep plus also skip kasan, while low memory variants combine thirty two bit DMA or plain DMA with kernel allocation.
The page order query for an area delegates to a shared area order helper.
